identity.title: Dry oral mucous membranes, tongue furrows, sunken eyes, dry axilla

technique.how: Inspect the oral mucosa and tongue with the mouth open: note dryness of buccal mucosa, longitudinal tongue furrows, and sunken eyes; palpate both axillae for moisture. Ask about mouth breathing and recent oral intake.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate light; patient able to open mouth.

interpretation.positive_finding: Dry mucosa with tongue furrows, sunken eyes or dry axilla supports hypovolemia, but positive LRs are modest.
interpretation.negative_finding: Moist mucous membranes and a tongue without furrows each argue against hypovolemia (LR- 0.3) in adults with vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake.
interpretation.pitfalls: Mouth breathing, oxygen therapy, anticholinergics and age-related changes dry the mouth without volume depletion; the reference standards in the source studies were heterogeneous.
interpretation.changes_what: Moist mucosa and unfurrowed tongue make prerenal hypovolemia less likely; dry findings favor a fluid trial but should be confirmed with urea/creatinine and electrolytes.

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolemia (dehydration) in patients with vomiting, diarrhoea or decreased oral intake
estimates.population: Adults, predominantly elderly ED patients with suspected dehydration
estimates.reference_standard: Chart-review dehydration severity rating or laboratory indices, per included study
estimates.quote: moist mucous membranes and a tongue without furrows argue against it (negative likelihood ratio, 0.3; 95% CI, 0.1-0.6 for both findings)

sources.citation: McGee S, Abernethy WB, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA 1999;281:1022-1029.
Gross CR, Lindquist RD, Woolley AC, et al. Clinical indicators of dehydration severity in elderly patients. J Emerg Med 1992;10:267-274.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Not validated for hemorrhagic hypovolemia; unreliable in mouth-breathers and patients on supplemental oxygen.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Do not let moist mucosa delay resuscitation in a hypotensive or oliguric patient.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Gross 1992 used a standardized 38-item exam; agreement statistics for individual signs are not reported in the abstract.

extraction_notes: Negative LR (0.3) for moist mucous membranes and unfurrowed tongue is from the RCE abstract; positive LRs and sens/spec for dry mucosa, sunken eyes and tongue furrows are in the RCE table (paywalled, not viewed) and left null. Gross 1992 abstract reports only P values (tongue dryness, furrows, dry mucosa, sunken eyes all correlate with severity, P<0.01), so no numbers extracted from it.
